title: loadpath handoff brief
description: `loadpath handoff`: the designer's exterior and component CAD in, a push-pad study out (handoff.py). Keep-outs per component with a clearance per component, insertFrom found from the assembly order, supports from what the part stands on, the plunger and its seat from the switch's geometry. The exterior is never changed.

any exterior through the intake (loadpath.exterior.load_exterior; `loadpath exterior`): a generated or scanned mesh is wrapped watertight, scaled and turned +z up

role.description: switch: the plunger is read off it; seat: what the switch bears on

installedOn.description: a component it is fitted to first and travels with (a switch on a flap, a connector on a board)

insertFrom.description: a hint, tried first; with fixed: true taken as given (an axis, a vector or a path of legs, as keepOut.insertFrom)

fixed.description: take insertFrom as given, no search

external.description: comes from outside after the part is closed (a plug): no clearance entry

clearance.description: a clearance entry for it (default true, except the switch, its seat and external parts)

pathTolerance.description: mm of interference allowed on its way in (a snap bead's reach)

assembly.description: component ids in the order they go in (default: as listed); components installedOn another travel with it

switch.description: the switch block of the study, with: component (the switch's id), gap (plunger to actuator, default 0.4 mm), trigger, travel, plungerRadius (default the actuator's), columnClearance (default 1 mm round the plunger), bearsOn (a seat component; default the one with role seat), clearanceMargin (default 0.2 mm), clearanceRegion (the nodes held to their room, default 'skin'; null for every node), and the presses, field, hold, unit... as in a study

rest.description: the side it stands on (default the press direction): supports there

restDepth.description: mm of the exterior's far side held (default 0.3)

keepOut.description: the designer's own clear zones, as given

pathTolerance.description: mm of interference allowed on a way in (crush ribs, a lip; default 0.25)

maxSlide.description: mm, longest first leg of a two-leg path (default 12)

box.description: Box: min/max corners, or center/size (axis-aligned), or center/size/axes (turned: size along the two axes given and their cross product).

radius.description: mm: round every edge and corner (axis-aligned boxes; default 0)

axes.description: the box's x and y axes as vectors (its z is their cross product); with center and size

cylinder.description: Cylinder or tube: end points p0/p1, or center/axis/length; radius r, optional rInner.

heightfield.description: One side of a surface given as heights over a plane: the points whose n.x is below (or above) h(u, v), h on a square grid in the plane's axes, bilinear between samples. A stepped or curved parting surface (loadpath split writes these).

axes.description: the plane's u and v axes

heights.description: heights[i][j] = h(u0 + i step, v0 + j step) along normal

mesh.description: A closed mesh: an STL/3MF/OBJ path relative to the study's folder (or a STEP file, .step/.stp, tessellated and healed; needs loadpath[step]), or inline stlBase64.

sdf.description: A sampled signed distance field: an .npz (distance, origin, pitch; mm, negative inside) relative to the study's folder, as loadpath.exterior.save_sdf writes it, or an OpenVDB level set (.vdb, from Houdini, Blender, nTop or `loadpath sdf`). How an SDF tool's shape (libfive, the sdf package, a field graph) comes in.

union.description: Several shapes acting as one region (a servo's four screw bosses).

intersect.description: Where all the shapes overlap: a half ring is a tube intersected with a box.

subtract.description: The first shape with the others cut away: a ring with a gap is a tube minus a box.

shape.title: a shape object (box, cylinder, tube, sphere, heightfield, mesh, sdf, union, intersect, subtract)
shape.description: A shape: box, cylinder (tube), sphere, heightfield, mesh, sdf, union, intersect or subtract. Units mm.
